speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: asked the Minister for National Development (a) how many cases of stray animal abuse in the community are reported in the past three years; (b) whether the numbers are rising each year; (c) what are the common types of abuse and most common types of animals affected; and (d) what is the Ministry's approach towards deterring abuse of stray animals.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: We take a serious view of all acts of animal abuse.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: NParks investigates all cases of feedback on animal abuse and will take enforcement action as appropriate.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Individuals who are found guilty of animal abuse can be charged under the Animals and Birds Act.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: In addition, NParks works closely with stakeholders such as animal welfare groups and veterinarians, to promote responsible interactions with animals.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: For example, NParks conducts outreach at pet-related events and community walkabouts and develops educational resources and programmes as part of its efforts.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Safeguarding the welfare of animals is a shared responsibility.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Members of the public can play their part by reporting suspected cases of animal abuse to NParks and providing information that might help to facilitate investigations.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Out of the cases of stray animal abuse over the past three years, how many animal abusers were caught?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: How can we better educate and create better awareness amongst community feeders about animal abuse, especially about signs and symptoms of abuse?

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: These injuries could have been caused by other circumstances, such as attacks by other animals, disease or accidents.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: So, for members of the public who come across such cases, please let NParks know.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: We have a 24-hour hotline at the animal response centre, 1800 476 1600, or go to the OneService app.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: And please include any information that might facilitate investigations.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: One, I understand we are reviewing the penalties for animal cruelty and abuse.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Could I just check what is the time frame for this review and when we could expect amendments to the Animals and Birds Act?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: And two, whether MND is also considering to include mandatory treatment orders as part of the penalties under the review?

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: The second question is around the mandatory treatment order.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: This is something that if the Member has views on, he can write to us with, as part of the consultation.
